When user_count is a positive multiple of limit (e.g. 100 with limit 50), this yields 3 instead of 2, so `showingLast` (propertyEqual of currentPage and totalPages) is false on the real last page, and clicking next clamps offset to user_count and requests an empty page. Off-by-one pagination logic introduced by this diff.

judged_text: totalPages computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts by one whenever user_count is a positive multiple of limit. A group with exactly 100 members and limit 50 displays totalPages 3 when only 2 pages exist; showingLast is false at the real last page, so the admin clicks next, offset is clamped to 100, the server returns an empty member array, and the page renders '3/3' with zero members — the admin is shown an apparently empty group.

record.issue_text: [BUG] totalPages computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts by one whenever user_count is a positive multiple of limit. A group with exactly 100 members and limit 50 displays totalPages 3 when only 2 pages exist; showingLast is false at the real last page, so the admin clicks next, offset is clamped to 100, the server returns an empty member array, and the page renders '3/3' with zero members — the admin is shown an apparently empty group.

adjudication.rationale: `totalPages` in `admin-group.js.es6` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50 => 3). With `showingLast` defined as `currentPage == totalPages`, the UI will not consider the real last page as last. Clicking `next` sets `offset` to `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)` (so it can become exactly `user_count`), and `Group.findMembers()` sends that `offset` to `/groups/:name/members.json`; in `GroupsController#members` the query `limit(limit).offset(offset)` will then return an empty set when `offset == total`, producing an empty member list on a bogus final page.
